person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers.

span.label: language model pre-training for transfer to NLP tasks
span.quote: Language model pre-training has been shown to be effective for improving many natural language processing tasks (Dai and Le, 2015; Peters et al., 2018a; Radford et al., 2018; Howard and Ruder, 2018).

span.label: computational-experiment
span.quote: In this section, we present BERT fine-tuning results on 11 NLP tasks.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: masked language modeling: randomly mask tokens and train the model to predict them from both left and right context, giving a deep bidirectional representation that transfers to many tasks via fine-tuning
span.quote: The masked language model randomly masks some of the tokens from the input, and the objective is to predict the original vocabulary id of the masked word based only on its context

span.label: Masking creates a mismatch between pre-training and fine-tuning because [MASK] never appears downstream.
span.note: what this limits: any account of what the pre-trained model has learned to expect: WE ARE CREATING A MISMATCH BETWEEN PRE-TRAINING AND FINE-TUNING, SINCE THE [MASK] TOKEN DOES NOT APPEAR DURING FINE-TUNING
span.quote: Although this allows us to obtain a bidirectional pre-trained model, a downside is that we are creating a mismatch between pre-training and fine-tuning, since the [MASK] token does not appear during fine-tuning.

span.label: The [CLS] vector is not usable as a sentence representation without fine-tuning.
span.note: what this limits: any use of the [CLS] vector as a sentence embedding without fine-tuning: THE VECTOR C IS NOT A MEANINGFUL SENTENCE REPRESENTATION WITHOUT FINE-TUNING, SINCE IT WAS TRAINED WITH NSP
span.quote: The vector C is not a meaningful sentence representation without fine-tuning, since it was trained with NSP.

span.label: Fine-tuning the large model was unstable on small datasets and required multiple random restarts.
span.note: what this limits: the reported small-dataset results: FOR BERT_LARGE WE FOUND THAT FINETUNING WAS SOMETIMES UNSTABLE ON SMALL DATASETS, SO WE RAN SEVERAL RANDOM RESTARTS AND SELECTED THE BEST MODEL ON THE DEV SET
span.quote: Additionally, for BERTLARGE we found that finetuning was sometimes unstable on small datasets, so we ran several random restarts and selected the best model on the Dev set.

span.label: The reported average is not the official score of the benchmark it is reported on.
span.note: what this limits: the GLUE averages quoted from this table: the authors state the Average column is slightly different from the official GLUE score because the WNLI set is excluded, so it is not comparable with an official GLUE average
span.quote: column is slightly different than the official GLUE score, since we exclude the problematic WNLI set

span.label: The pre-training objective is an existing task under a new name, which the authors state.
span.note: what this limits: any claim of novelty for the masked LM objective: the authors note the same procedure is often referred to as a Cloze task in the literature, citing Taylor 1953
span.quote: We refer to this procedure as a “masked LM” (MLM), although it is often referred to as a Cloze task in the literature

span.label: The paper's central adjective is one the systems it is compared against also use.
span.note: what this limits: any comparison of bidirectional models: the authors distinguish their deep bidirectional pre-training from a shallow concatenation of independently trained left-to-right and right-to-left language models, so the word alone does not separate the architectures
span.quote: BERT uses masked language models to enable pretrained deep bidirectional representations. This is also in contrast to Peters et al. (2018a), which uses a shallow concatenation of independently trained left-to-right and right-to-left LMs

span.label: the Cloze task of Taylor 1953 - delete a word from a passage and ask a reader to supply it - made the pre-training objective of a transformer language model as the masked language model
span.quote: BERT alleviates the previously mentioned unidirectionality constraint by using a “masked language model” (MLM) pre-training objective, inspired by the Cloze task (Taylor, 1953).

span.label: the two pre-training approaches compared by applying them to the same CoNLL-2003 named entity recognition task
span.note: eliminates: a difference between the approaches that is really a difference in the task each was tried on
span.quote: In this section, we compare the two approaches by applying BERT to the CoNLL-2003 Named Entity Recognition (NER) task (Tjong Kim Sang and De Meulder, 2003).

span.label: extends → Peters et al., 2018a and Radford et al., 2018
span.quote: Unlike recent language representation models (Peters et al., 2018a; Radford et al., 2018), BERT is designed to pretrain deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.

span.label: extends → Radford et al. (2018)
span.quote: Unlike Radford et al. (2018), which uses unidirectional language models for pre-training, BERT uses masked language models to enable pretrained deep bidirectional representations.

span.label: builds-on → Vaswani et al. (2017)
span.quote: BERT’s model architecture is a multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder based on the original implementation described in Vaswani et al. (2017) and released in the tensor2tensor library.

span.label: builds-on → the Cloze task (Taylor, 1953)
span.quote: BERT alleviates the previously mentioned unidirectionality constraint by using a “masked language model” (MLM) pre-training objective, inspired by the Cloze task (Taylor, 1953).
